title: Reduce complete H25 certificate qualification time by 28%
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

The complete frozen historical H25 `scripts/complex_network.py` CLI, with retained exact observations, takes **28.636256246 seconds median wall / 28.46 seconds CPU** with the unchanged PR5929 native GF(2) kernel, versus **39.686181760 / 39.58** for Python. The reductions are **27.8433% wall and 28.0950% CPU**. Both exceed the declared 15% and repeat-spread gates across six fixed cold BCCBBC processes. Every candidate pays fresh compilation/link/load, independent finite controls and the same full output work.

This extends the earlier side-segment assessment to the actual unchanged full caller: all original assertions, exact parameter/logarithm/guard/gate checks, the real 19-file upstream verifier, certificate write and both stdout lines execute. It is tooling for a frozen historical conditional certificate. No uninstrumented bare-CLI factor, current selected-frontier result, PR5864 improvement, mathematical construction or new kappa is claimed. The separate further 15% PR5864 objective remains unmet.

## Task and overlap

Task `replay-runtime`, refined scope `frozen-H25/complete-historical-caller/native-GF2`. Base/current canonical main: `19fdb086ea96af9a9f87936a2b888e10af4ed810`, freshly fetched before this round and again before submission; priority revision 8. Immutable input ancestor: `7f9c2985de167e95d159040eee26fc03c1e27fb6`; publication head: `4f4159820c37f01d245784d1186bd51fcbc8ebb6`. The diff contains only 125 added files under `research/gf2-full-network`.

This answers the explicit complete-caller next question in [PR5929](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5929), retaining its seven engine files byte for byte. The earlier investigation claim is [here](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5929#issuecomment-6451967873). Bounded open-PR H25 searches found PR5929 and the separate [PR5972 key audit](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5972); newest handoffs were also inspected. This is limited overlap coverage, not a novelty proof. Historical source, selected-record context and exact source ancestry remain explicit in TASK/SOURCES.

## Validation

| Complete qualification | Python median | Native median | Reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Wall seconds | 39.686181760 | 28.636256246 | 27.8433% |
| CPU seconds, compiler included | 39.58 | 28.46 | 28.0950% |

Savings of 11.049925514 wall / 11.12 CPU seconds exceed maximum within-arm ranges of 4.533797564 / 3.48. All six samples, including the slower C3, remain. The diagnostic anchor is excluded; no benchmark sample was dropped or rerolled.

Every run matches the complete original certificate bytes and stdout, lossless ordered typed return, 58,143,622-byte side witness, 59,959 rank records and 238,685 ordered complement observations. The complement stream hashes 55,839,507 bytes; the archive retains its receipt rather than the stream itself. Six lossless canonical payloads retain 60,831,231 logical bytes. Exact full certificate SHA-256 is `1f763d95c7ff163aa71d13cd82784f16665be8afb21f75e76941e2119562098f`; typed return SHA-256 is `542e4fd73d38b88122d1bf0fffa5f3b092cc4681a14012162daef47e89363cfd`.

Fresh normal/optimized finite checks, complete read-only Git-free C correctness replay, streaming canonical checks, metadata, committed bytes/executable modes/source ancestry, and the committed export with all 42 declared inputs pass locally. The dense independent oracle, 5,329 small ordered complement pairs, 585 Gram cases, 64/65-bit boundaries, types/fallback and live source/binding controls are retained. The initial entry import failure and a later publication-only read-only cleanup failure are preserved with their repairs. Scientific code and fixed samples did not change during packaging. All 123 protected files match the tested read-only stage.

Local measurements: Linux x86-64, Core i7-4790, CPython 3.12.3 / GCC 13.3. One parent serial runner; 180s per scientific command, 1 GiB sampled group RSS; no automatic retries. Publication wrappers add archive authentication, so their separate correctness runs do not establish another wrapper performance factor. Hosted exact-head correctness [run40577785495](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40577785495) **passed** at `4f4159820c37f01d245784d1186bd51fcbc8ebb6`: 676 shared tests with 22 skips, selection of only this package, all four registered checks (finite normal/O, complete C correctness, canonical transport), and clean tracked-input/index diffs. This supersedes the preparation-time pending CI entries in committed VALIDATION.json. Hosted correctness does not rerun or establish the six-run local performance factor.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/gf2-full-network
# One explicit fresh complete replay; B chooses Python:
python3.12 -B research/gf2-full-network/replay.py C /tmp/gf2-full-new-evidence
```

No dependency installation is required; Linux CPython 3.12, existing compiler/headers and GNU time are needed. Full runs require original assertions; optimized mode is finite-only. See README, VALIDATION and evidence/COMPLETE-GATE.json.

Adjacent native/GMP/FLINT precedents remain credited: PR5168, PR5382, PR2853 and PR3143. Chris R / Clear1nsight with substantial OpenAI Codex implementation and user-requested Astra xhigh source design and separate static reviews. Parent alone executed compiler/scientific work. Finite engineering evidence is not human or proof-kernel acceptance of the multiplication theorem.

## Open next questions

This scoped full historical caller evaluation is complete. Another caller or runtime needs its own complete source/output contract and paid validation before any performance transfer; TASK records the first step and blockers. No further construction or timing reroll is justified by this result. Mathematical streams, unrelated feeds and automations remain paused.
